children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures fell back on Tuesday, giving up most their gains from Monday.

Feeling the pressure Sharp losses in crude oil spurred the turnaround in canola with more pressure coming from declines in Chicago soyoil and soybeans, as well as European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil.
An analyst said there may have been a technical selloff in canola.
The November canola contract closed slightly above its 20-day moving average but remained well above its other averages.
Weather Prairie temperatures are to reach the high teens to low 20s Celsius with no rain. That will aid farmers in making progress in an already delayed harvest.
Loonie The Canadian dollar was weaker on Tuesday afternoon, with the loonie at 71.07 U.S. cents, compared to Monday's close of 71.32.
Contracts There were 54,956 canola contracts traded on Tuesday, compared to 50,142 on Monday. Spreading accounted for 28,794 contracts traded.
